answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a willow as the anchor of the cost.
